video.title: NBA Fantasy Basketball Rankings Best & Worst Case Scenarios for Every Round [2026/27]

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through the first 10 rounds of Fantrax ADP. For each round he names the player with the tightest range of outcomes and the player with the widest. The ranges come from his projections and historical variance in each category, using the middle 60% of outcomes (20th to 80th percentile). Injuries and minutes are not included. Jokic, Durant, Kawhi, Sabonis, Kyrie, Gobert, Hartenstein, Sharpe and Darryn Peterson come out as the narrow-range options. Haliburton, Trae Young, Brunson, Knueppel, Anunoby, Sarr, Pritchard, Norman Powell, Dybantsa and Reed Sheppard have the widest ranges. He strongly advises avoiding Alex Sarr, Payton Pritchard and AJ Dybantsa at their ADPs. His closing point is that small changes, like one extra steal a week, can move a player's rank a lot, so you should draft knowing a player's range and decide when you want safety and when you want upside.

rules.text: Fantasy leagues are small samples. Do not treat a player's average as something that will repeat exactly.
rules.quote: we deal with small sample sizes in most fantasy leagues, roto excluded.

rules.text: Putting too much of your team into high-variance categories leaves you open to strange losses.
rules.quote: putting all your eggs into a high variance basket leads you susceptible to weird losses.

rules.text: Pick between upside and safety based on your roster. If you have already taken several risky swings, lean toward players with a narrower range.
rules.quote: I've done a lot of cracks, so therefore maybe I want to get a guy where the range is narrower

rules.text: Steals are a highly variable category. Even elite steals players can drop to 0.7 or 0.8 per game in a season.
rules.quote: We know that steals are a highly variant category and he's terrible at them.

rules.text: Further down the board, ranks are packed tightly. A small drop in one stat can cost a player 10 or more spots.
rules.quote: instead of 6.7 assists you average 6.4 four and you fell 12 spots. Everything is incredibly tight

rules.text: In later rounds (9 and 10), the downside of most players is just being useless. Take upside flyers on players who could reach the top 50.
rules.quote: can anyone be top 50 here? Have a look

rules.text: Base fantasy value on each player's current situation, not on how much you like them as a player.
rules.quote: everything in how I look at at fantasy is about what's the current situation.

rules.text: Whether you choose an upside pick or a safe pick depends on what the rest of your team looks like.
rules.quote: that is depending on what sort of player you want, what's your team looking like?

rules.text: Tiny changes move ranks a lot. One extra steal a week (about 0.3 per game) can be worth around 15 spots, and one extra made basket per game around 10 spots.
rules.quote: your steals go up by.3 and your fantasy rank improves by 15 spots.

rules.text: Nothing in a projection is guaranteed. Understand which categories are more variable and decide when you are drafting for safety and when for a big upside hit.
rules.quote: Work out when you're drafting for safety and when you're drafting for that big dinger.
